headline: Chips and Crude Lead Friday's Split Session as Strait Tensions Cloud the Week Ahead
body_html:
Markets closed Friday's session on an uneven note, with advancing issues narrowly trailing decliners — 260 up against 285 down across a universe of 549 names. Energy and Materials emerged as the clear leaders, gaining 1.38% and 1.22% respectively, as mounting disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz — where traffic has slowed materially following threats of additional economic pressure on Iran and a reported attack on a tanker near the waterway — put a fresh bid under commodity-linked equities. Semiconductors added 1.13%, buoyed by double-digit moves in MaxLinear (+10.68%) and solid gains in Sandisk (+7.39%) and AMD (+6.50%).

The day's losers were concentrated in Software, which shed 1.38% as a group. N-able slid 6.52% and ZoomInfo fell 6.03%, extending a recent pattern of pressure on subscription-software names. Applied Materials dropped 5.12%, a notable exception to the broader semiconductor strength, while Homebuilders (-0.60%) and Consumer (-0.31%) also finished in the red.

Heading into the new week, geopolitical risk dominates the macro backdrop. Ongoing Israeli operations in Lebanon, Houthi disruption at Yemen's Mocha port, and unresolved tensions around Iran's Hormuz posture give commodity desks plenty to monitor. Marijuana policy is gaining unexpected traction as a midterm issue, while Indonesia's magnitude-7.7 earthquake adds a humanitarian dimension that markets will watch for any supply-chain spillover.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Bottleneck Tightens as Iran Standoff Deepens
briefs.body: Tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has slowed further after the United States threatened additional economic pressure on Iran, and the UAE reported that an attack targeted an ADNOC-linked vessel in the waterway. The incidents are fueling energy-market anxiety heading into a week with few obvious diplomatic off-ramps.

briefs.headline: Lebanon Strikes Intensify, Casualty Toll Mounts
briefs.body: Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon resulted in at least eleven deaths, according to Lebanese authorities, with a separate strike killing seven in a reported single incident. The escalating toll raises the prospect of broader regional destabilization and is being watched closely by risk desks alongside Hormuz developments.

briefs.headline: Houthi Attack Forces Yemen Port to Suspend Operations
briefs.body: The director of Yemen's Mocha port confirmed a suspension of all operations following Houthi strikes on the facility. The closure adds another chokepoint to an already stressed regional shipping picture and could complicate commodity flows through the Red Sea corridor in the days ahead.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Names Dominate Friday's Leaderboard
briefs.body: MaxLinear surged 10.68% to top the session's gainers, with Sandisk adding 7.39% and AMD climbing 6.50%. The moves pushed the broader Semiconductors sector up 1.13% for the day, even as Applied Materials bucked the trend with a 5.12% decline that analysts are likely to scrutinize for equipment-cycle signals.

briefs.headline: Software Sector Slides as N-able and ZoomInfo Lead Losses
briefs.body: N-able fell 6.52% and ZoomInfo dropped 6.03% on Friday, dragging the Software group down 1.38% — the weakest sector performance of the session. The selloff extended recent weakness in subscription-model technology names and contrasted sharply with the day's strength in hardware-adjacent semiconductors.

briefs.headline: Taliban Mark Five Years in Kabul Amid Deepening Humanitarian Alarm
briefs.body: The Taliban marked the fifth anniversary of their return to power in Afghanistan as international aid organizations issued renewed warnings about a deteriorating humanitarian situation. The milestone draws renewed attention to aid-funding pipelines at a moment when a separate United Nations finding linked a hostage ransom of roughly fifty million dollars to militant financing in Mali.
